title: Internal condensed action categories and injective derived infrastructure
statement:
Fix the small coherent profinite site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, morphisms and all section sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $J,H$ be topological groups. Write $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ for internal $R$-modules with a natural $\underline J$-action by linear automorphisms [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

The presheaf $\underline J$ is a sheaf of groups. The action-site equivalence identifies $\mathcal A_R(J)$ with module sheaves over the ring $R_J$ on the small action site: forgetting action creates sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels and detects zero objects. Both $\mathcal M_R$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The formula
$$\Gamma_{R,J}M(S)=\{m\in M(S)\mid \forall(V\to S),\ \forall g\in C(V,J),\ g\cdot m|_V=m|_V\}$$
defines a sheaf of $R$-modules and a normalized adjunction $T_J\dashv\Gamma_{R,J}$: the forward transpose restricts the codomain to this invariant subsheaf and the inverse composes its inclusion. Forgetting action detects exactness; trivial inflation, restriction along every continuous group homomorphism $u:H\to J$, and restriction along every condensed ring map $R\to R'$ are additive and exact.

Every complex in the action category has a K-injective resolution (a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ such that every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null homotopic); every bounded-below complex has a bounded-below resolution by injective modules which is K-injective. The ordinary total right derived functor $F_J=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] is computed by $\Gamma_{R,J}I$, and its canonical computation unit is invertible on K-injectives, in particular on bounded-below complexes of injectives. It is additive and triangulated. There is the canonical derived adjunction $D(T_J)\dashv F_J$, induced by the above Hom bijections; its unit and counit commute with the fixed signed K-injective shifts. Exact trivial, group and scalar restrictions descend termwise with their canonical signed shift comparisons.

proof.text: For a finite jointly surjective profinite cover $\{S_i\to S\}$, compatible continuous maps $h_i:S_i\to J$ define a unique set map $h:S\to J$: compatibility on $S_i\times_S S_j$ makes its value independent of the chosen preimage. The surjection $q:\coprod_i S_i\to S$ is a quotient map by [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient], since its source is compact and $S$ is Hausdorff. The glued map is continuous because $h q$ is continuous on each summand and $q$ has the quotient topology. The empty cover gives the unique map from the empty set. Pointwise multiplication and inversion preserve continuity and commute with restriction; hence $\underline J$ is a group sheaf. Postcomposition with a continuous group homomorphism $u:H\to J$ gives a morphism of these group sheaves.

source.place: Tags 08YD (lemma-closed-map), 0AAU (lemma-closed-morphism-quotient-topology); elementary descent along their quotient map

proof.text: Use the abelian sheaf tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; its strong monoidal sheafification gives the monoidal local-equivalence hypothesis of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The latter identifies internal $R$-modules with module sheaves, identically on underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restrictions. It therefore identifies the action data and equivariant maps in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] with the sectionwise $\underline J$-equivariant module sheaves. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] to the small coherent profinite site, the group sheaf from step 1 and $R$. The base site has finite limits and all the values are in the specified coefficient universe. Its small ringed action site and $R_{\underline J}$ give the asserted equivalence; write $R_J=R_{\underline J}$. The same result gives precisely sectionwise kernels, sheafified sectionwise cokernels, and zero detection after forgetting action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), categorical input: translation from internal modules and the existing small action-site presentation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation] to this site and $\underline J$. Its category is the action category of step 2 with exactly the specified addition, so it is Grothendieck abelian and its forgetful functor detects exactness. Apply the same statement to the terminal group sheaf: its unique action identifies its objects and maps with $\mathcal M_R$, giving the Grothendieck structure there. For the morphism $\underline H\to\underline J$ of step 1 its exact additive inflation is restriction along $u$. For $\underline J\to1$ it is trivial inflation from $\mathcal M_R$. Thus both restrictions and trivial inflation are additive and exact. All applications allow the zero ring and the trivial group.

source.place: Paragraph (3), generic Grothendieck and exact-inflation infrastructure, specialized to continuous-map group sheaves

proof.text: Through the identification of step 2, which keeps sections, restrictions and action operators, an object of $\mathcal A_R(J)$ is an $\underline J$-equivariant module sheaf on this site. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-product-fixed-adjunction] to the small coherent profinite site, which has finite limits, the ring sheaf $R$ and the group sheaf $K=\underline J$ of step 1 (with $L$ the trivial group sheaf), and take $P=K$. With $p=g\in C(V,J)$ its displayed submodules $M^P(S)$ are exactly the sections in the formula for $\Gamma_{R,J}M(S)$. Its statement gives that they form an $R$-module subsheaf, naturally in $M$; that restricting equivariant maps defines the additive functor $\Gamma_{R,J}=\Gamma_P$ with its sectionwise injective inclusion $i_P$; and the natural additive adjunction $T_J=T_P\dashv\Gamma_{R,J}$ whose forward transpose keeps every section map and restricts its codomain to the invariant submodule and whose inverse composes with $i_P$. The image of $i_P$ is exactly the fully fixed sections of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], so this is the normalized invariants datum specified there. The statement covers the trivial group sheaf and the zero ring.

source.place: Paragraph (3), normalized invariant subsheaf and adjunction, from the existing fixed-subsheaf adjunction node

proof.text: For a condensed ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$, [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] keeps the abelian sheaf and maps unchanged and sets $r m=\varphi(r)m$. An $R'(S)$-linear action remains $R(S)$-linear, so scalar restriction also acts on the equivariant categories. It is additive. The kernel formula of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is unchanged. So is the cokernel: the section quotient has the same abelian presheaf, and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] defines its module sheafification on the sheafification of that abelian presheaf; its unique extended action restricts along $\varphi$. Therefore the ordinary module scalar restriction preserves kernels and cokernels and finite biproducts, hence is exact. In the action categories forgetting identifies its underlying functor with this one, so the exactness detection of step 3 proves its exactness there. This uses neither flatness nor surjectivity of $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), section on change of rings; elementary comparison of the same kernel and abelian-sheaf cokernel

proof.text: Both categories are Grothendieck abelian by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] to each: every complex has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] they also have enough injectives. For a bounded-below complex, [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] gives a bounded-below quasi-isomorphic complex of injective objects; [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] makes that complex K-injective. In particular this gives the required equivariant resolutions, in the action category itself.

source.place: Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck); bounded-below replacement and K-injectivity in the cited existing Mathlib leaves

proof.text: The source and target of the additive $\Gamma_{R,J}$ have the K-injective resolutions of step 6. The computation assertion of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] therefore gives $F_J(K)\cong\Gamma_{R,J}I$ for each K-injective resolution $K\to I$, and its computation unit is invertible on every K-injective $I$. This includes bounded-below injective complexes by step 6. Apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to these same two abelian categories and this additive functor: its unbounded K-injective right derived functor has the canonical shifts and is triangulated. In particular it is additive, as part of the triangulated-functor structure.

source.place: Tags 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); triangulated structure also in the cited existing project theorem

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], the right adjoint $\Gamma_{R,J}$ of the exact $T_J$ sends K-injectives to K-injectives. For any complex $X$ of $\mathcal M_R$ and K-injective action complex $I$, [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A_R(J))}(T_JX,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal M_R)}(X,\Gamma_{R,J}I)$ with the original transpose formulas. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] these are the corresponding derived Hom sets: both targets are K-injective. Using step 7 and exact termwise $D(T_J)$, this is the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A_R(J))}(D(T_J)X,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal M_R)}(X,F_JK)$. The natural bijections define the derived adjunction, and their formulas show it is induced by the specified underived Hom bijections. They apply to all derived objects since every object has a complex representative and every $K$ has the resolution of step 6.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] separately to the exact additive trivial inflation, group restriction, and scalar restriction from steps 3 and 5. Each descends termwise, has the canonical signed shift comparisons, and is triangulated. In the complex shift by $n$, both routes have differential $(-1)^nF(d)$; thus these are precisely the stated signed comparisons, with no change of convention.

source.place: Tags 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), 014X (lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category); full signed factorization supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] with $C=\mathcal M_R$, $D=\mathcal A_R(J)$, $L=T_J$ and right adjoint $\Gamma_{R,J}$. The abelian categories and K-injective resolutions come from steps 3 and 6, additivity and exactness from steps 3--4. Its conclusion concerns the canonical derived adjunction induced from precisely this underived adjunction, computed on K-injectives as in step 8, and retains the fixed K-injective shift of step 7. Consequently both its unit and counit commute with those shifts. This supplies the normalization asserted in the last paragraph without choosing a replacement shift on $F_J$.

No new nodes, no SGA. Accepted the statement correction from continuous map u to continuous group homomorphism u. The counterexample checks: on C2 with the sign action, the constant map to the non-identity element makes 1_H act by -1, so u^* is not an action. The parent restriction-calculus node and def-sfb-condensed-action-module already use homomorphisms. Checked steps 1-3 and 7-12. Step 1: the gluing quotient only needs the profinite base S to be Hausdorff; J may be non-Hausdorff. Step 2: strong monoidal sheafification gives monoidal local equivalences, and the action-site presentation hypotheses hold (small site with finite limits, group sheaf, universes). Steps 3 and 7: Grothendieck structure, exact inflation and exact scalar restriction (no flatness needed). Steps 8-10: K-injective and bounded-below resolutions, the derived functor, and the Hom bijection, with no cycle with the termwise step 11. Step 12: the fixed-shift adjunction hypotheses hold. Edge cases pass: empty S, trivial J, zero ring. The five tool_uses are accepted as generic K-injective/adjunction black boxes. FIX (C5): old steps 4-6 re-prove the existing same-unit base node lem-sfb-sheaf-product-fixed-adjunction. That node states the invariant subsheaf (identical formula), the additive functor with its injective inclusion, and the adjunction with the same transposes; it does not reach the item. The corrected item merges those steps into one step 4 that cites it with P=K=J, renumbers steps 5-10 and updates proof_deps and the tool_uses step numbers. The statement is unchanged.
